editorial:
Step into 1980s Gotham and meet Arthur Fleck, a lonely man who wants to make people laugh but keeps getting pushed aside. His life is rough, his mind is fragile, and every bad day pulls him closer to something darker. The city feels tense, dirty, and ready to snap, so you feel the pressure building around him. You watch a sad clown become a symbol for angry people, and that makes the whole story feel heavy but hard to look away from.

Joaquin Phoenix gives a wild, unforgettable performance, and the music and camera work make every scene feel sharp. The movie is slow in spots and very dark, so it may not be for everyone. If you like character studies, crime dramas, and intense acting, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Arthur fully becomes Joker and dances down the stairs as Gotham riots around him. He kills a talk show host on live TV, gets arrested, then escapes when angry crowds crash the police car. Later, he is in a hospital, laughing and leaving bloody footprints, while a doctor asks about a joke. You realize he may be imagining parts of his story, and his violent legend has already inspired the city.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark character studies and intense crime dramas.
